inherits.rule: UAK0 outcomes O05-O07, consumers C13-C14, seam S12, cell Z05 and routes D16-D17 stay authoritative with their owners. ENC0 refines them: every outcome below names its UAK0 parent, and every boundary row in the ledger names D16 or D17 as parent when it splits one. No UAK0 or UAK1 row gains a second owner.

law.rule: Every position a Rust core fact stores, caches, keys or compares is a UTF-8 byte offset or half-open byte range in one named coordinate domain. A value whose domain or unit cannot be named is a defect; there is no 'UTF-8 unless evidence suggests otherwise'.
Domains are disjoint. No arithmetic, comparison or assignment crosses domains; a crossing goes through the owner of the map between them.
UTF-16, UTF-32 and line/column forms exist only inside the adapter that speaks them. Each crossing converts exactly once, in the adapter, against the exact content snapshot the position indexes.
Every wire position names its encoding and line/column base, as a tag on the value or as a fixed, versioned property of the wire contract. A doc comment alone is not a contract.

No layer retains a document's coordinates re-expressed in a requester encoding. A boundary index built for one content snapshot and dropped with it, holding byte line starts and computing requester columns on demand, is not a mirror. The TypeScript provider's own UTF-16 line table (LI2) is the provider wire's index, not a mirror of the internal domain.

A position off a valid boundary of its domain (inside a UTF-8 sequence or surrogate pair, past the end, inverted, overflowing) is a typed failure. Nothing clamps, saturates or snaps to a character or token. Only a rule the wire itself defines (LSP 3.17 character past line length) is applied by its adapter, for read-only queries; edits and secondary links refuse.
Generated sources are not ASCII. An ASCII fast path must equal the general path; it is never an assumption that swaps byte and UTF-16 units.
A requester encoding never enters a prepared-artifact key, semantic-flight key, cache key or stored fact.

A mapped position is valid only against the exact content and map revision it was computed on (ContentId, MapRevision, the certified engine query's content_hash/map_hash). A changed basis rejects the position; it is never re-mapped approximately. PER0D consumes this for invalidation.

A line/column form's terminator set belongs to its wire: LSP 3.17 breaks at 
, 
 and lone ; TypeScript also at U+2028/U+2029; the V3 source-map split is the emitted 
. Two line/column forms convert into each other only through byte offsets of one content snapshot.

domainRulings: ENC0T reuses the existing verter_span names SourceByteOffset, SourceByteRange, GeneratedByteOffset and GeneratedByteRange: it moves their definitions into coord/, re-exports them at their current paths, adds EmbeddedByteOffset and EmbeddedByteRange and the checked API. No second type with an existing name.

Construction from a raw integer is explicit and named. No From, Into, Deref or Add<u32> between a domain type and an integer; no cross-domain arithmetic. Range constructors reject end < start instead of relying on saturating_sub in len().
CD2 stays RelativeSpan. The embedded types are only for cooked or derived text, where an offset is not a byte of the authored file.
Span stays the serialised authored-source span. PartialGeneratedSpan and GeneratedSpan have no production consumer outside verter_span and the verter_parser re-export; recorded as P31, not migrated.

lineIndexRule: One index per wire contract. A request builds at most one index per (content snapshot, wire) and converts every endpoint through it. A new line/column form needs a row here, not a private table. Test-only and tooling copies (compiler tsc/ide/ssr tests, verter_bench examples, verter_dx_baseline::materialize) are outside the production population.
